name: Proto-Oceanic
orthography_note: Orthography of Ross (1988, 1989) with pʷ and kʷ added (Table 1.3, p. 27).
notes: Parent is PMP: the source rejects the interstages PEMP and PCEMP (pp. 40-46). It also argues that early POc kept a third, prenasalised obstruent series (ᵐb, ⁿd, ᵑg; also ⁿr, ñj) from PMP nasal + obstruent clusters, merged with the voiced series in POc as conventionally reconstructed (pp. 33-39), and reports a proposal by Lynch (2022) to revise the vowels (pp. 39-40). Neither revision is in the inventory entered here.

name: Proto-Micronesian
orthography_note: Orthography of Jackson (1986) with s for his d and S for his z, and with y and Z added; ŋ for the velar nasal, ñ for the palatal nasal, superscript ʷ for the labiovelars (Bender et al. 2003a: 2-3).
notes: Consonants from the PMc rows of Tables 2-3 of Bender et al. (2003a: 4-5). The pages entered give no vowel inventory (vowel correspondences are referred to Jackson 1983: 321-323 and Goodenough 1992); the five vowels are those used in the vowel tables of Blumenfeld (2022b: 711-712). In Bender et al. PMc is the ancestor of Kosraean, Kiribati, Marshallese and the Pohnpeic and Chuukic languages (Figure 1 (p. 3, adapted from Jackson 1983: fig. 6)); Blumenfeld (2022b: 687), following Hughes (2020a, b), adds Nauruan. The Glottolog node Micronesian (micr1243) includes Nauruan.

name: Nauruan
orthography_note: Surface forms; stress, the allophonic change t, d > ts, dz before i, and gemination of sonorants are not shown (Blumenfeld 2022b: 689).
notes: Treated as a Micronesian language descending from PMc, following Hughes (2020a, b); Jackson (1986) had excluded it from nuclear Micronesian (Blumenfeld 2022b: 687). It shares the merger of *s and *S with all Micronesian languages except Kosraean, but the source calls conclusions about subgrouping premature (pp. 687, 717). Fewer than 200 items are given etymologies and many changes are not fully regular (p. 686). The layer of Kiribati loans (section 3) is not entered.
